claims.label: Re-Leasing / Mitigation Costs
claims.note: Landlord's work, tenant-improvement allowances, and leasing commissions incurred to re-lease the space -- usually actual, invoiced costs, so recovery tends to run close to the amount claimed.

claims.label: Property Damage / Repairs
claims.note: Reduced for a typical 10-20% normal-wear-and-tear haircut.

claims.label: Breach of Quiet Enjoyment / Constructive Eviction
claims.note: Fact-intensive claim, informed by comparable cases rather than a formula -- see cited cases.

claims.label: Attorney's Fees
claims.note: Posture-tiered flat-dollar estimate (went to trial) -- fees are driven by procedural effort, not claim size, for a typical matter in this range; a large or unusually complex matter can run higher.

extractedFacts.wrongfulLockoutCitation: 735 ILCS 5/9-101 et seq. (Forcible Entry and Detainer Act) requires judicial process for eviction; self-help is prohibited for Illinois commercial landlords. No confirmed statutory damages multiplier for a wrongful commercial lockout -- tenant's remedy is actual damages, which can include lost business revenue, emergency relocation costs, and property/inventory losses, plus attorney's fees and costs.

outcome.description: After a bench trial the court rejected the tenant's breach claim (and dismissed unjust enrichment), found the tenant and guarantors liable, and entered judgment for the landlord of $852,421.64: $365,255.76 rent, taxes and utilities through April 30, 2022; $111,910.38 construction expenses; $327,626.48 lump-sum liquidated damages; $28,000 brokerage fees; and $19,629.02 prejudgment interest. It later awarded $202,034.79 in attorney fees and costs without an evidentiary hearing. The Appellate Court affirmed liability and damages except the $28,000 brokerage fee, which it reversed, and reversed and remanded the fee award for an evidentiary hearing.
outcome.attorneysFeesOnAppeal: reversed and remanded for evidentiary hearing
outcome.finalNote: Affirmed except the $28,000 brokerage-fee component, which was reversed; fee award remanded.
